area: data-efficiency techniques for PC12 segmentation (n≈70 labeled + unlabeled pool + incoming batch 2)

candidates.name: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 or B/14 (fine-tuned on own unlabeled pool)
candidates.what_it_does: Pretrained ViT features (142M images, no labels). Fine-tune the checkpoint on your unlabeled PC12 pool, then use it as frozen backbone + light segmentation head, or as a feature extractor (kNN density maps as a free auxiliary supervision signal).
candidates.pc12_fit: High for the fluorescence channel; usable for phase contrast but ImageNet-pretrained features are phase-contrast-agnostic, hence the domain fine-tune.
candidates.neurite_support: None built in (feature-level only); helps boundary generalization, not topology.
candidates.license: Apache-2.0 (code + weights) — verified in repo README
candidates.compute: Fine-tuning ViT-S/14 or B/14 fits one 24 GB GPU (official fine-tune configs target single-node multi-GPU but scale down); pretraining from scratch is out of reach (repo: ~1 day on 32 A100-80GB for ViT-L/16).
candidates.small_data_fit: Strong: SSL gains are largest exactly when labels < ~100; fine-tuning on a few hundred unlabeled images is the documented recipe.
candidates.effort: 2-4 day spike (fine-tune on pool, attach U-Net head, compare vs ImageNet-pretrained ResNet baseline).
candidates.notes: Do NOT pretrain from scratch. If unlabeled pool < ~300 images, expect modest gains; fine-tune with low LR (1e-5..1e-4) and keep the original checkpoint as fallback.

candidates.name: Cell-DINO (Meta, fluorescent cell microscopy self-supervision)
candidates.what_it_does: DINOv2 variant pretrained on Human Protein Atlas single-cell, HPA FoV, and Cell Painting; domain-adapted features for cell fluorescence. Weights via access request.
candidates.pc12_fit: Fluorescence channel only — not trained on phase contrast. Best used as a frozen feature branch for the fluorescence input, not the main encoder.
candidates.neurite_support: Pretraining crops are single-cell (no long neurites) → no topology specialization.
candidates.license: CC-BY-NC (code) + FAIR noncommercial (weights) — fine for a thesis, blocks commercial release
candidates.compute: Inference/frozen-use only: trivial on 24 GB. Training variant: ~2 days on 4 A100-80GB nodes (per README) — skip.
candidates.small_data_fit: Potentially better in-domain start than generic DINOv2 for fluorescence; unverified for phase contrast and PC12 morphology.
candidates.effort: 1 day to request + eval features vs DINOv2.
candidates.notes: Gated download + NC license + niche fit; only worth it if fluorescence channel is a first-class input.

candidates.name: FixMatch (and FixMatch-pytorch)
candidates.what_it_does: Pseudo-label from weak aug kept only above a confidence threshold; train to match it under strong aug. Verified abstract: 88.6% CIFAR-10 with just 40 labels — evidence it works far below our label count. Ablations (per abstract) show the confidence threshold is the load-bearing piece.
candidates.pc12_fit: Medium: code is classification-oriented; per-pixel adaptation for segmentation is a known but manual port (~1-2 weeks).
candidates.neurite_support: Weak: thin structures are never 'confident' at borders; naive per-pixel thresholding drops exactly the neurite pixels that matter. Needs a morphological gate (e.g., only pseudo-label interior/eroded regions).
candidates.compute: Two forward passes per unlabeled sample per step; trivial on 24 GB.
candidates.small_data_fit: Credible at 70+unlabeled, but engineering cost is high for 2 students.
candidates.notes: The simpler pseudo-label self-training loop (below) captures most of the gain at 1/4 the cost; FixMatch's consistency term is the part you'd be paying for.

candidates.name: Pseudo-label self-training loop (teacher → threshold → spot-check → retrain)
candidates.what_it_does: Train strong teacher on 70 images → predict unlabeled pool → keep only high-confidence regions (per-pixel p>~0.95 AND skeleton sanity: predicted component size/length in plausible range) → human spot-check ~5 images → add to training, 2-3 rounds max.
candidates.pc12_fit: Directly targets the 50-500 image unlabeled pool; rounds are cheap overnight jobs.
candidates.neurite_support: Add a topology gate before accepting pseudo-labels: reject regions where skeleton has broken fragments or Betti count mismatch vs plausible cell topology — this is the cheap way to make pseudo-labeling neurite-safe.
candidates.code: hand-rolled (~100 lines on your existing trainer)
candidates.compute: one teacher inference pass per round; trivial.
candidates.small_data_fit: Good: 2-3 rounds + spot-check gate keeps confirmation-bias risk low; with 70 labeled seeds the teacher is already decent, which is the regime where self-training works.
candidates.notes: Simplest credible semi-supervised option; stop after 2-3 rounds (gains saturate, error compounds). Log acceptance rate per round as a health metric.

candidates.name: CRITIC (Zhao et al., CVPR 2020, unsupervised domain adaptation for cell instance segmentation)
candidates.what_it_does: Critic-guided UDA for instance segmentation of cells; relevant if the unlabeled pool / batch 2 comes from a different acquisition setting (exposure, well, timepoint) than the 70 labeled images.
candidates.pc12_fit: Only if the pool is cross-domain; otherwise plain self-training suffices.
candidates.code: UNVERIFIED — no working repo/paper URL found in this pass (multiple candidate URLs 404'd).
candidates.small_data_fit: designed for scarce-labels regimes; but unverifiable here = unusable in week 1.
candidates.notes: Re-resolve the exact arXiv ID / repo before citing; do not plan on it until then.

candidates.name: Simple Copy-Paste (Ghiasi et al.) + CP2
candidates.what_it_does: Paste instance masks onto random backgrounds. Verified abstract: +0.6 mask AP COCO over prior SOTA and large LVIS rare-class gains (baseline beat LVIS 2020 challenge entry by +3.6 mask AP on rare classes) — rare-class result is the closest analogy to our thin/rare neurite foreground. CP2 (2203.11709) turns the same mechanism into a pixel-wise contrastive pretraining objective (78.6% mIoU VOC with ResNet-50 after fine-tune).
candidates.pc12_fit: Adapt as RIGID-UNIT copy-paste: extract each cell as (body + attached neurites) crop from the 70 labeled images (~hundreds of donor units), rotate the whole unit by a random angle, feather the alpha boundary, paste 1-2 units per background patch. Track the applied rotation so pasted-instance angle labels stay exactly consistent.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes IF done as rigid units (rotate image+mask together = labels stay valid). Never paste a neurite stub that would cross a patch edge, and never exclude... DO exclude the donor's own image as paste target and keep donor/recipient within the same CV fold split (no leakage).
candidates.code: method is ~100 lines with existing masks; CP2 repo URL not stated in verified abstract (unverified)
candidates.small_data_fit: Excellent — the single best label-multiplier at n=70: instance count grows without any labeling.
candidates.notes: Cap pastes at 1-2 per patch and keep ~30-40% of patches real-only, else the model learns a synthetic prior (illumination halo around pastes). Intensity-match donors to recipients.

candidates.name: STARDOM (diffusion-based augmentation for microscopy, as named in project brief)
candidates.what_it_does: Reported as diffusion-generated variants of microscopy images + masks for segmentation training.
candidates.pc12_fit: Unverified — could not locate the paper or a public repo via arXiv API or GitHub search in this pass.
candidates.code: UNVERIFIED — no repo found (searched 'stardom' on GitHub API incl. in:name/in:description; nothing microscopy-related).
candidates.notes: Treat as a rumor until a verifiable URL lands. If it exists, its risk profile equals the HistoSmith/MSDM/DualDiT category below: high cost, unproven small-n gain.

candidates.name: Synthetic data via joint image-mask diffusion (HistoSmith, MSDM, DualDiT)
candidates.what_it_does: Latent diffusion models generating realistic image+mask pairs for cell/nuclei/histology segmentation. HistoSmith (2502.08754): joint layout+mask+image LDM, helps underrepresented classes. MSDM (2510.09121): morphology/color/metadata-conditioned generation for cell & nuclei segmentation. DualDiT (2607.29337): dual-output DiT; FID 56.14, expert panel misclassified 46% of synthetics as real, downstream Dice/IoU improved but only modestly.
candidates.pc12_fit: Would need training a new joint image-mask model on 70 pairs — thin training set for the generator itself.
candidates.neurite_support: All three are cell-body/nuclei-centric; none targets long tubular neurites.
candidates.code: UNVERIFIED in this pass (no repos confirmed).
candidates.compute: 48 GB for a few days per generator experiment.
candidates.small_data_fit: Poor as a first move: honest cost/benefit — the tractography-synthesis study (2606.26898) reports synthetic-ONLY training fails and mixed real+synthetic needs 3x less annotation; i.e., generators only work as a garnish on top of real supervision, not a replacement. At n=70 the expected downstream gain is ~1-3% Dice for 3-6 weeks of student-time.
candidates.notes: This is the trap: high cost, small uncertain gain, zero neurite-specificity. Revisit only if batch-2 labeling is capped AND cheap wins already exhausted. The cheaper sibling recipe (instance-preserving auto-aug + mask-conditioned pix2pix, IAAA/SAAA 2602.00949) is the one to copy if synthesis is ever needed.

candidates.name: Deep Active Learning via MC-dropout uncertainty (neuropoly/deep-active-learning)
candidates.what_it_does: U-Net + dropout MC sampling → per-image uncertainty → label the most uncertain first. Verified abstract: on real histology datasets of 14 and 24 images, 3 uncertainty-selected samples reached max Dice where 15 random samples did not — the exact small-n regime we're in, and direct evidence AL works at our scale.
candidates.pc12_fit: Rank the 50-500 unlabeled / batch-2 images by uncertainty; label top K (K = what the lab can afford, e.g. 10-20); also rank crops within images.
candidates.neurite_support: Entropy is weak for thin structures (a broken long neurite contributes little pixel-mass entropy) — pair with a topology term (see bold ideas).
candidates.code: https://github.com/neuropoly/deep-active-learning (cited in paper abstract; repo itself unverified this pass)
candidates.compute: MC passes over pool: hours on 24 GB.
candidates.small_data_fit: Excellent — the paper's datasets are smaller than ours.
candidates.notes: Also use rareness-aware scoring (2507.17359 shows contrastive pretraining + rareness-aware acquisition helps under class imbalance) — practically: weight uncertainty by predicted neurite-pixel share.

candidates.name: nnU-Net v2
candidates.what_it_does: Fully automatic 2D/3d U-Net pipeline: patching, augmentation (incl. elastic), ensembles, self-configuring. Already a known prior in the project.
candidates.pc12_fit: Fastest path to a solid supervised baseline in days; use its 2D config on 512 patches.
candidates.neurite_support: Weak: Dice-optimized, under-segments thin tubes; must be augmented with soft-clDice in the loss to serve neurites.
candidates.small_data_fit: Robust defaults + elastic augmentation make it a strong small-data baseline; 5-fold CV by image is manual but standard.
candidates.notes: Week-1 supervised reference that everything else must beat.

candidates.name: clDice / soft-clDice loss
candidates.what_it_does: Similarity computed on intersection of masks and their morphological skeletons; verified abstract: differentiable soft-clDice, topology preservation up to homotopy equivalence, tested on 5 datasets incl. neurons; improves connectivity, graph similarity, volumetric scores.
candidates.pc12_fit: Purpose-built for exactly the failure mode we care about: broken/fused neurites.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes — this is the tubular-structure method.
candidates.code: paper provides the formulation (2003.07311); standalone implementation existence unverified — expect 1-2 days to implement (skeletonize with scikit-image + differentiable morph ops).
candidates.compute: skeletonization per batch element: minor overhead.
candidates.small_data_fit: Acts as a structural inductive bias = regularizer, which is most valuable at n=70.
candidates.notes: Use as ADD-ON to Tversky/BCE, not a replacement (w=0.1-0.3). You already chose clDice as an eval metric — training with it makes the metric aligned with the objective.

candidates.name: Tversky loss (asymmetric F1)
candidates.what_it_does: Weights FP vs FN independently (alpha, beta); standard fix for small/elongated foreground drowned by background. Train with Tversky (alpha=0.3, beta=0.7 → penalize FN less than FP or vice versa) + soft-clDice + small BCE.
candidates.neurite_support: Yes at the pixel level; no topology awareness (that's clDice's job).
candidates.code: scikit-medimage / any custom loss; trivial to implement
candidates.notes: Primary reference is Tversky (1984) Psychol. Rev. + widespread segmentation use; no arXiv checked this pass (unverified link).

candidates.name: Focal loss (Lin et al.)
candidates.what_it_does: Down-weights easy negatives to focus on hard examples (verified abstract, RetinaNet motivation: extreme FG-BG imbalance).
candidates.pc12_fit: Secondary: with only 2 classes, Tversky+clDice already addresses imbalance; focal mostly helps dense multi-class detection.
candidates.notes: Try only if Tversky+clDice still over-predicts background; don't stack all three from day 1 (loss soup hides which term helps).

candidates.name: Style augmentation (Ginsburger, MoNuSeg)
candidates.what_it_does: Style-transfer-based augmentation reducing CNN texture overfitting; verified abstract: improves segmentation on MoNuSeg with few labeled data.
candidates.pc12_fit: Cheap proxy for exposure/illumination variability across wells and the future batch 2 (likely a different instrument session).
candidates.notes: Histogram matching + random brightness/contrast/gamma is the 90% solution in 1 hour; style aug is the +10% if intensity variability dominates your CV variance.

candidates.name: IAAA / SAAA instance-aware augmentation (CAR-T/NK synapse, fluorescence + brightfield)
candidates.what_it_does: Verified abstract: IAAA = optimized augmentation policies applied instance-preservingly to microscopy images with masks; SAAA = diffusion-based mask generator + Pix2Pix image synthesizer aligned to those masks; both improve detection/segmentation on a limited annotated microscopy dataset.
candidates.pc12_fit: Closest published evidence that this exact recipe (instance-preserving aug + mask-conditioned pix2pix) works on small microscopy datasets — the blueprint to copy if you ever go the synthetic route.
candidates.neurite_support: instance-preserving (whole-object) rather than pixel-level — compatible with rigid-unit pasting.
candidates.notes: If synthesis is ever greenlit, do SAAA-lite (pix2pix on mask-conditioned crops) instead of full latent diffusion.

bottom_line: Week-1 cheap wins, in order: (1) histogram-matched preprocessing + 5-fold image-level split with leak guards; (2) nnU-Net-v2-style baseline with elastic + rotation augmentation and neurite-rich 512-px patch oversampling, loss = Tversky (alpha 0.3/beta 0.7) + soft-clDice (w~0.2) + BCE; (3) rigid-unit Copy-Paste from the 70 labeled images with rotation-tracked angle labels and ≤2 pastes/patch, donors never crossing fold boundaries. The two highest-value spikes are a pseudo-label self-training loop (ensemble-confidence + skeleton/Betti sanity gate + 5-image human spot-check, 2-3 rounds max) and uncertainty-based active learning over the unlabeled pool/Batch 2 (MC-dropout + Betti-disagreement term — entropy alone is blind to thin structures; the 14/24-image histology evidence shows AL pays at exactly our n). Skip: FixMatch/CRITIC/Mean-Teacher-style fancy SSL (engineering cost exceeds expected gain at n=70) and any diffusion-based image synthesis (verified literature shows synthetic-only fails, mixed gains are 1-3% for weeks of work, and no generator targets tubular neurites). The one genuinely novel, deliverable contribution is the topology-aware AL + known-answer morphometric test set from rotation-tracked pasting — cheap, publishable, and directly aligned with your Betti/clDice metrics.
